I have been farming this same land in Quzhou my whole life. I am 61 now. My father farmed it before me. Everyone here in the village grows winter wheat then summer corn — that is the rotation we do. Two harvests a year, steady income, and I know every step by heart.

I have about 8 mu of contracted land. I am not going to try something new at my age. Cotton prices collapsed years ago and I gave that up. Vegetables take too much labor and my knees are not what they were. Wheat and corn — that is my plan, same as last year, same as the year before.

For the wheat I will get the improved seed from the township supply station, the same Jimai variety I used last season, it did well. I will rotary till before planting in October. I put down compound fertilizer as a base, then top-dress urea at jointing in spring. I water three times: once before winter to help the roots set, once at jointing, once when it heads. I spray herbicide early and then hit the aphids before harvest. I should get around 450 jin per mu — I mean kg, sorry, about 450.

For summer corn I plant right after I combine the wheat in June, no-till, straight into the stubble. I use Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed, same as everyone. I fertilize once at planting and side-dress at the big bell stage. If July is dry I irrigate once, but usually the rains help. One spray for corn borers if I see them. Harvest in late September.
